# Pulmonary Embolism Rule-out Criteria (PERC)

> A bedside rule-out screen for adults in whom a clinician already judges the pre-test probability of pulmonary embolism (PE) to be **low**. It records eight objective criteria — age, heart rate, oxygen saturation, unilateral leg swelling, haemoptysis, recent surgery or trauma, prior venous thromboembolism, and exogenous oestrogen use — and asks whether the clinician's gestalt pre-test probability is low. When **all eight criteria are satisfied** *and* the pre-test probability is **low**, the patient is **PERC-negative**: PE can be excluded without a D-dimer or imaging. If any criterion fails, or the pre-test probability is not low, the patient is **PERC-positive** and further workup (D-dimer and/or imaging) is warranted.
